c: Ce problème est difficile à résoudre.

traiter.e: Inherited from Middle French traicter, from Old French tretier, traitier, traiter, from Latin tractāre (“to pull, manage”), from the past participle stem of trahō (“to draw, pull”) (cf. tractus, whence French trait).

reconnaître.e: Inherited from Old French reconoistre, from Latin recognōscere. By surface analysis, re- + connaître.
c: C'est grand de ta part de reconnaître que tu as tort.
Hatalı olduğunuzu kabul ettiğiniz için çok büyüksünüz.
Tu as tellement changé que j'ai du mal à te reconnaître.
Sen o kadar çok değiştin ki seni zorlukla tanıyabiliyorum.

fromage.e: Inherited from Middle French froumaige, formage, from Old French formage, from Early Medieval Latin fōrmāticum, from Latin fōrma (“mould”). Compare Occitan formatge.

essence.e: From Old French, from Latin essentia. Sense 2 very likely from Latin edō (“eat”), in the sense of 'what is eaten, fuel'.

ayant.e: Old French aiant, from Latin habēns, the present participle of habēre. Cognate to Spanish habiente, Italian avente, Catalan havent.
c: J'aime les histoires ayant une fin triste.
Venez, s'il vous plaît, en ayant faim.

côte.e: Etymology tree Latin costabor. Old French coste Middle French coste French côte Inherited from Middle French coste, from Old French coste, borrowed from Latin costa.
c: Ils ont marché côte à côte.
Je suis de la côte Est.

chaleur.e: Inherited from Old French chalor, from Latin calōrem m.
c: Il fait une putain de chaleur.
Le lait tourne avec la chaleur.
Quel est l'objet de ta question ?
La mort de son mari fut sa renaissance.
L'annihilation donne naissance à ma renaissance.

europe.e: Borrowed from Latin Eurōpa, from Ancient Greek Εὐρώπα (Eurṓpa), a character in Greek mythology.

supplier.e: Modified based on the original Latin prefix sup-, from Old French souploier, sosploier, from Latin supplicāre.
c: Ne me force pas à supplier !
Je vais acheter la première tournée.
Roger travaille du matin au soir.
Bununla ilgili olarak, ben suçlu değilim.
As-tu le moindre retour nous concernant ?
Bizim için herhangi bir geri bildiriminiz var mı?

souffrir.e: Inherited from Old French sofrir, from Vulgar Latin *sufferīre, from Latin sufferre.
c: Mon bras me fait encore souffrir.
Souffrir est le destin de l'homme.

fusil.e: From Old French fuisil, foisil, from Vulgar Latin *focīlis (petra), from Latin focus. Compare Italian fucile.

gardien.e: From Old French guardian, guardein (“protector, guard”), from an earlier *gardenc, the first root deriving from guarder and the second from Proto-Germanic *-ingaz, cf the similarly-formed Italian guardingo .

vote.e: Borrowed from English vote. Doublet of vœu.

c: Si tu te fais de nouveaux amis, n'oublie pas les anciens.
Yeni arkadaşlar edinirsen , eski arkadaşlarını unutma.
Je ne suis pas forcément d'accord avec vous sur ce point.
Ben o konuda zorunlu olarak seninle aynı fikirde olamam.

herbe.e: Inherited from Old French erbe, herbe, from Latin herba, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʰreH₁- (“to grow, become green”).
c: Mon chat adore l'herbe à chat.
Il y a un plan B.
Je devais choisir entre A et B.
Ben A ve B arasında bir seçim yapmak zorunda kaldım.

menteur.e: Inherited from Middle French menteur, from Old French menteor, menteür, menterre. By surface analysis, mentir + -eur. May correlate to a Vulgar Latin *mentitōr, mentitōrem, from Latin mentior.

vif.e: Inherited from Middle French vif, from Old French vif, from Latin vīvus (“alive, living”), from Proto-Italic *gʷīwos, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *gʷih₃wós (“alive”).

c: Est-ce que je m'adresse à Taylor ?

adulte.e: Learned borrowing from Latin adultus (“grown up”), perfect participle of adolēscō (“to grow up”) (the present participle of which - adolēscens (“growing up”) - gave French adolescent).

siècle.e: ), a borrowing from Latin saeculum. The expected inherited form would be *sieil.

attente.e: From Old French atente, inherited from Latin attendita.

c: Tu n'as pas lu les rapports ?
Je veux ces rapports, dans l'heure, sur mon bureau.
Şu raporları bir saat içinde masamda istiyorum.

piscine.e: From Latin piscīna (“fishpond; swimming pool”), from piscis (“fish”), from Proto-Indo-European *peysk-.

lendemain.e: Univerbation of l' (an apocopic form of la, la before a vowel) + endemain, itself a univerbation of en and demain. Compare Italian l'indomani.
c: Il n'y a pas de lendemain.
Il est devenu riche du jour au lendemain.
O, bir gece içinde zengin oldu.

fumer.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dʰewh₂- Proto-Indo-European *-mós Proto-Indo-European *dʰuh₂mós Proto-Italic *θūmos Proto-Italic *fūmos Latin fūmus Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂ Proto-Indo-Europ…

coach.e: Unadapted borrowing from English coach. Doublet of coche.
c: Tom n'a pas besoin d'un coach.
Elle aimait le tennis et devint coach.
Tenisi sevdi ve tenis koçu oldu.

élever.e: From é- + lever, or borrowed from Latin ēlevāre.
c: Élever un bébé est un travail difficile.

chair.e: Inherited from Middle French chair, char, from Old French char, charn (earlier carn), from Latin carnem, carō, from Proto-Italic *karō, from Proto-Indo-European *ker-, *(s)ker-. Doublet of carne.
c: Tu es ma chair et mon sang.

magique.e: Learned borrowing from Latin magicus, itself borrowed from Ancient Greek μαγικός (magikós). By surface analysis, magie + -ique.

chaîne.e: Inherited from Middle French chaisne, from Old French chaene, chaiene, caiene, inherited from Latin catēna. Doublet of cadène and catène.

chèque.e: Inherited from Middle French check, checque, from English check (“cheque”). First attested in 1774. The current spelling dates back as early as 1803.

réseau.e: From Middle French réseau, resel, from Old French resel, from Old French reiz, rez; equivalent to rets (“fishing net”) + -eau.
c: Je n'ai pas pu me connecter au réseau.

enfance.e: Inherited from Old French enfance, borrowed from Latin īnfāntia, from īnfāns (“unable to speak”).

c: Je ne veux profiter de personne.

science.e: Inherited from Middle French science, from Old French science, a learned borrowing from Latin scientia, from sciēns + -ia.

crâne.e: ), a borrowing from Medieval Latin crānium.

jaloux.e: Inherited from Old French jalous, from Late Latin zēlōsus, from zēlus, from Ancient Greek ζῆλος (zêlos, “zeal, jealousy”). Compare Italian geloso, Spanish celoso.

arrestation.e: From Middle French arrestation. Equivalent to arrêter + -ation.

laver.e: Inherited from Old French laver, from Latin lavāre, from Proto-Indo-European *lewh₃- (“to wash”).
c: Je l'ai vu laver la voiture.
Il est en train de laver la voiture.

caisse.e: Inherited from Middle French caisse, borrowed from Occitan caissa, from Latin capsa. Compare the etymological doublets châsse and casse.

cris.e: Clipping of Christenaux (now Knistenaux), from Cree Kenisteniwuik (the name of a Cree village).

cri.e: Inherited from Middle French cri, from Old French cri, a deverbal derived from crier (“to cry”). Compare English cry.

traité.e: Inherited from Old French traitié, traiete, derived from traiter after Latin tractātus.

promesse.e: Inherited from Old French, borrowed from Medieval Latin or Late Latin prōmissa (“promise”), from Latin prōmissum (“promise”), from promittō (“to send forth; to promise”).

sénateur.e: Learned borrowing from Latin senātōrem. By surface analysis, sénat + -eur.
c: Il avait servi comme député et sénateur.
Le sénateur a un emploi du temps très chargé cette semaine.
Senatörün bu hafta çok zorlu bir takvimi var.

sucre.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ḱorkeh₂ Proto-Indo-Iranian *ćárkaraH Proto-Indo-Aryan *śárkaraH Sanskrit शर्क॑रा (śárkarā) Gandhari 𐨭𐨐𐨪 (śakara)bor. Middle Persian 𐭱𐭪𐭥 (šakar)bor. Arabic سُكَّر (sukkar)bor.

c: Je déteste la couleur de ces murs.
De quelle couleur sont les murs dans ta chambre ?

représenter.e: From Old French représenter, from Latin repraesentāre. Morphologically re- + présenter.
c: Vous ne représentez rien pour moi.
Benim için hiçbir şey ifade etmiyorsun.
Emma Watson est une ambassadrice de bonne volonté d’ONU Femmes.
Emma Watson, BM Kadın İyi Niyet Elçisidir.

cloche.e: From Medieval Latin clocca, from Proto-Celtic *klokkos (see also Welsh cloch, Old Irish cloc), ultimately imitative. Related to Old English clucge, Low German Klock (“bell, clock”), German Glocke, Swedish klocka.
c: Ters giden bir şey mi var?
Je savais que quelque chose clochait.
Merkezi haber alma teşkilatı seni izliyor.

étudier.e: From Middle French estudier, from Old French estudier.

trompe.e: From Middle French trompe, from Old French trompe, from Frankish *trumpa, *trumba (“trumpet”), ultimately from an imitative Germanic word akin to Old Dutch drumba, trumba (“trumpet, horn”), Old High German trumba, trump…

tromper.e: Inherited from Middle French tromper, from Old French tromper (“to tramp, trump, delude”, literally “to play on the trumpet”), from trompe (“trump, trumpet”), from Frankish *trumpa (“trump, trumpet”), from a common Germ…
c: Tout le monde peut se tromper.

chute.e: From a merger of Old French cheüe, chue (from Vulgar Latin *cadūta) and cheoite (from Vulgar Latin cadecta), both feminine past participles of cheoir, whence modern choir (compare chu).
c: Ma grand-mère a peur de faire une chute.
Le prix de la viande a chuté.
Les prix des bons du Trésor ont chuté.

demi.e: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *dimedius, from Latin dīmidius (“half”), derived from dis- (“apart; in two”) + medius (“middle; centre”).

plainte.e: Inherited from Old French plainte, pleinte (from the feminine past participle of plaindre, pleindre), corresponding to a Medieval Latin plancta, from Latin planctus.

grand-chose.e: Compare Italian granché (literally “great thing”) for a similar construction, also used only in negative sentences.

c: Je me suis perdu en venant ici.
Tom s'est perdu en venant ici.

chouette.e: ] From Middle French chouette, from Old French choete, diminutive from choe (“jackdaw”), from Frankish *kâwa.

c: Karen est en colère avec moi.

département.e: Inherited from Old French departement, from departir + -ment.
c: Où se trouve le département enfants ?
C'est le patron de notre département.

peinture.e: Inherited from Old French peinture, from Vulgar Latin *pinctūra, alteration of the classical Latin pictūra, under the influence of the verb it's derived from, pingō.

opinion.e: From Middle French opinion, from Latin opīniōnem.

c: Je voulais juste faire un geste.

gaffe.e: From Old Occitan gaf (“clasp”), from Gothic 𐌲𐌰𐍆𐌰𐌷 (gafah, “clasp”, noun), from 𐌲𐌰- (ga-, intensifier) + 𐍆𐌰𐌷𐌰𐌽 (fahan, “to catch”).

empire.e: Inherited from Old French empire, from Latin imperium.

empirer.e: Attested in Old French as empirier, empoirier, equivalent to en- + pire (“worse”) + -er. Compare Spanish empeorar.
c: Bu sadece onu daha kötü yapar.
Je suis ton plus grand fan.

poitrine.e: Inherited from Old French poitrine, peitrine, from Vulgar Latin *pectorīna, derived from Latin pectus. Gradually replaced pis, now meaning udder. Cognate with Spanish pretina (“waistband”).
c: J'ai une douleur à la poitrine.
À quand remonte vos dernières vacances ?
En son ne zaman bir tatil yaptın?
À quand remonte la dernière fois que Tom a fait ça ?
Tom onu en son ne zaman yaptı?
Elles ont essayé de me remonter.

aventure.e: From Vulgar Latin *adventūra, from Late Latin adventūrus, from Latin adventus.

maquereau.e: Inherited from Middle French macquereau, maquereau, maquerel, from Old French maquerel, of uncertain origin.

abby.e: Borrowed from English Abby in the 20th century.

barre.e: From Middle French barre, from Old French barre (“beam, bar, gate, barrier”), from Vulgar Latin *barra, of uncertain origin.
c: Ma barre d'espace ne fonctionne pas très bien.
Le ballon a frappé la barre transversale.

foyer.e: Inherited from Vulgar Latin *focārium, nominalization of the Late Latin adjective focārius, from Latin focus (“hearth”).

cauchemar.e: Inherited from Middle French cauchemare, from Old French cauquemare. By surface analysis, cauque + mar. Compare Walloon tchôcmwår.

soupe.e: From Middle French souppe, from Old French sope, supe, soupe, from Late Latin suppa (“sopped bread”), from Proto-Germanic *supô.

souper.e: From Middle French soupper, from Old French soper, derived from supe, sope (“soup”) (modern French soupe).

jus.e: Inherited from Middle French jus, from Old French jus, from Latin iūs (“gravy, broth, sauce”).

prêtre.e: Inherited from Middle French prestre, from Old French prestre (nominative form, compare provoire), from Latin presbyter, from Ancient Greek πρεσβύτερος (presbúteros), from πρέσβυς (présbus, “elder, older”).

corde.e: Inherited from Middle French corde, from Old French corde, borrowed from Latin chorda (“gut”), from Ancient Greek χορδή (khordḗ, “string of gut, cord”).

champion.e: Inherited from Old French champion, from Medieval Latin or Late Latin campiōnem, campiōnem (“champion, fighter”), from Frankish *kampijō, from Proto-Germanic *kampijô, based on Latin campus (“level ground”).
c: Tu es le champion, n'est-ce pas ?

somme.e: Inherited from Old French somme, sume, borrowed from Latin summa.

c: La conférence commence à trois heures.
Est-ce votre première conférence à Paris ?

commissaire.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ḱe? Proto-Indo-European *ḱóm Proto-Italic *kom Proto-Italic *kom- Latin con- Proto-Indo-European *mey-?
c: Le suspect a menti au commissaire.

crème.e: Inherited from Middle French chresme, from Old French cresme, from Late Latin crama, a Transalpine Gaulish word influenced by Latin chrisma (modern French chrême), from Ancient Greek χρῖσμα (khrîsma).

c: Plus d'une centaine de personnes est venue ici.
Elle a des centaines de livres.

joueur.e: Etymology tree French jouer Proto-Indo-European *-tōr Proto-Italic *-tōr Latin -(ā)tōrem Old French -or Middle French -eur French -eur French joueur From jouer + -eur.

c: J'ai vu Tom dans le couloir.
Elle est dans le couloir de la mort.

horreur.e: Inherited from Old French horror, borrowed from Latin horror, from the verb horreo (“to shiver”). The feminine gender's origin is unclear.

propriété.e: Inherited from Old French proprieté, itself borrowed from Latin proprietās. Compare propreté.

admettre.e: Inherited from Old French admettre, borrowed or adapted from classical Latin admittere, infinitive of admittō, based on French mettre.

matériel.e: Inherited from Old French materiel, from Late Latin māteriālis (“material, made of matter”), from Latin māteria (“wood, material, substance”) from māter (“mother”).
c: Ils n'avaient pas de bon matériel.

foule.e: Inherited from Middle French foule (“group of men, people collectively”), alteration (due to Middle French foule (“act of treading”)) of Old French foulc (“people, multitude, crowd, troop”), from Early Medieval Latin fu…
c: Il a disparu dans la foule.

réaction.e: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin reactio.
c: Je ne comprends pas votre réaction.

ennuyer.e: Inherited from Old French enoiier, from Late Latin inodiāre.

laura.e: Borrowed from Late Latin Laura. A Latinate variant of Laure.

c: Ma femme travaille dans un pub à côté.

hiver.e: From Middle French hyver, from Old French iver, from Late Latin hībernum.

manteau.e: Inherited from Latin mantellum, diminutive of mantum. Compare Italian mantello.

pis.e: Inherited from Old French piz, peiz (“chest, udder”), inherited from Latin pectus, from Proto-Italic *pektos, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peg- (“breast”).

débile.e: Learned borrowing from Latin debilis. The original sense of "weak" was lost to faible.

conseiller.e: Old French conseillier, from Latin cōnsiliātor. Equivalent to conseil + -ier.
c: Peux-tu me conseiller un bon jeu ?
İyi bir oyun tavsiye edebilir misiniz?
Il n'a pas d'amis pour le conseiller.
Ona tavsiyede bulunacak hiç arkadaşı yok.

humanité.e: Learned borrowing from Latin hūmānitās. By surface analysis, humain + -ité.

studio.e: From Italian studio. Doublet of étude.
c: Elle dirige un studio de danse.
Je n'allume pas la lumière dans mon studio la nuit.

lapin.e: From Middle French lapin, alteration of lapereau, with change of suffix after connin, a word it replaced.

désert.e: Inherited from Old French desert, borrowed from Latin dēsertum (according to the Trésor de la Langue Française).

c: Il est dingue d'une fille qui s'appelle Julie.
Julie adında bir kız için deli oluyor.
Dan est venu accueillir Julie à six heures.

boutique.e: Inherited from Middle French boutique, borrowed from Old Occitan botica, from Latin apothēca, from Ancient Greek ἀποθήκη (apothḗkē). Doublet of bodéga.

fonds.e: Inherited from Old French funz (“cultivated or developed land”), from Latin fundus. Doublet of fond.
c: Il est à court de fonds.
Je n'ai pas de fonds à la banque.

discussion.e: From Late Latin discussiōnem, from Latin discutiōnem.

incendie.e: Ca. 1600, borrowed from Latin incendium. Perhaps influenced by Occitan incendi (in the 16th c. ), which may be inherited or is at least a much earlier borrowing.

c: Le vent a couché beaucoup d'arbres.

surface.e: From Middle French surface, equivalent to sur- + face, a calque of Latin superficiēs.
c: Je ne suis pas sûr de quand il va faire surface.
Onun ne zaman döneceğinden emin değilim.
La surface de cette table est lisse.

curieux.e: Borrowed from Latin cūriōsus (“careful, attentive, inquisitive”).

ascenseur.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂éd Proto-Italic *ad Proto-Italic *ad- Latin ad- Proto-Indo-European *skend-der.

mars.e: Inherited from Old French mars, from Latin (mensis) mārtius.

abri.e: Inherited from Middle French abri, from Old French abri (“a place where one is sheltered from the elements or harm”), from abrier (“to cover”), from Late Latin abrigō (“to cover, shelter”), from a- + brigō, from Frankis…

larme.e: Inherited from Old French larme, lerme, from Latin lacrima, from Old Latin lacruma, dacrima, dacruma, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *dáḱru-.

impliquer.e: Borrowed from Latin implicāre. Doublet of employer.

pardonner.e: Inherited from Old French pardoner, from Late Latin perdōnāre.

soi.e: Inherited from Old French sei, accented form of se, from Latin sē (in accented position), from Proto-Indo-European *swé (reflexive pronoun). More at se. Cognate with Italian sé, Portuguese si, Spanish sí.

marine.e: From marin, from Latin marīnus, derived from mare (“sea”).
c: Mon père était dans la Marine.

marin.e: Inherited from Middle French marin, from Old French marin, from Latin marīnus.

c: Une lettre a été trouvée près du cadavre.
Il y a un cadavre dans le coffre de la voiture.

front.e: Inherited from Old French front, from Latin frontem, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰron-t-, from *bʰren- (“project”).
c: Il a été trois mois au front.
Ils ont perdu la guerre sur le front Est.
Uniquement de l'eau, je vous prie.
Il y a uniquement un bus toutes les deux heures.
Sadece her iki saatte bir otobüs vardır.

rare.e: Borrowed (in this form) from Latin rārus. Compare the inherited Old French rer, rere.

gloire.e: From Middle French gloire, from Old French gloire, glorie, borrowed from Latin glōria.

c: Le gang est devenu la famille de Sami.

communauté.e: Inherited from Old French com(m)unalté, alteration after comunal (see communal) of communité, itself borrowed from Latin communitātem.
c: Tom était bien connu dans la communauté.

déclaration.e: Borrowed from Latin dēclārātiōnem (accusative singular dēclārātiōnem).

c: Mon nom de famille est Jones.

frontière.e: From front + -ière. Compare Catalan and Spanish frontera; Portuguese fronteira; Italian frontiera.

haïr.e: Inherited from Middle French haïr (“to hate”), from Old French hair (“to hate”) (compare Old French enhadir (“to become filled with hate”)), from Frankish *hattjan (“to hate”), from Proto-Germanic *hatjaną (“to hunt, ru…
c: Je ne peux pas te haïr.

prénom.e: Learned borrowing from Latin praenōmen. By surface analysis, pré- + nom.

liaison.e: Inherited from Old French, from Late Latin ligātiōnem, derived from Latin ligō (“bind”), or formed from lier + -aison based on the Latin word. Compare also Old Occitan liazó, liazon.

cérémonie.e: From Latin caerimōnia, from caelum + munia.
c: Il était présent à la cérémonie.

ho.e: (This etymology is missing or incomplete. Please add to it, or discuss it at the Etymology scriptorium.

vélo.e: Clipping of vélocipède (“velocipede”), which is now obsolete.

poupée.e: Inherited from Middle French poupée, from Old French poupee, popede (cf. also Medieval Latin *pupāta), or Vulgar Latin *puppa (with the French suffix -ée later added), ultimately from Latin pūpa (“girl; doll, puppet”).

navire.e: Inherited from Middle French navire, from Old French navirie, variant of navilie, probably from Vulgar Latin *navilium (compare Old Occitan navili), alteration of Classical Latin navigium (whence also Old French navoi,…
c: Le capitaine contrôle tout le navire.
Patrick ne sait pas écrire correctement.
Bob l'Éponge et Patrick sont amis.

ménage.e: Inherited from Middle French mesnage, from Old French manage, mainage, from manoir, maneir, maindre, from Latin manēre.
c: Fais le ménage dans ta chambre.
Il a une femme de ménage.

bouton.e: Inherited from Middle French bouton, boton, from Old French bouton, boton (“button, bud”), from Vulgar Latin *bautōnem, accusative of bautō, from Frankish *bautō (“that which pushes up, bump, knob”), from Proto-West Ger…
c: Ne touche pas à ce bouton !

acteur.e: Inherited from Middle French acteur, from Latin actor.

c: Bu bir köpek ve midilli gösterisi.

julia.e: From Latin Iūlia. A Latinate variant of Julie.
c: C'est ma sœur. Elle s'appelle Julia.
Bu benim kız kardeşim. Adı Julia.
Où est Julia ? Elle est dans sa chambre.

mardi.e: Inherited from Latin Mārtis diēs, variant of diēs Mārtis (literally “day of Mars”).

juré.e: Inherited from Old French juré, from Latin iūrātus. Doublet of jurat.
c: Ils ont juré de garder le secret.
Onlar onu bir sır olarak saklayacağına yemin etti.

médecine.e: Inherited from Middle French medicine, from Old French medecine, borrowed from Latin medicīna. Replaced the inherited Old French form mecine.
c: En quelle année de médecine êtes-vous ?

lourd.e: Inherited from Middle French lourd, from Old French lorz, lourt, from Late Latin lurdus, lordus, probably from Latin lūridus (“sallow”), possibly influenced by Frankish *lort (“crooked, clumsy”); related to Old English…

c: Tom est chargé de ce projet.

bite.e: From Old Norse biti (“beam, girder”), from Proto-Germanic *bitô, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰeyd- (“to split”).

soudain.e: Inherited from Old French sodein, from Vulgar Latin *subitānus, from Latin subitāneus (“sudden”), from subitus.
c: Son départ soudain nous a tous surpris.

baisser.e: Inherited from Old French baissier, from Vulgar Latin *bassiāre, from Late Latin bassus.

rompre.e: Inherited from Middle French rompre, from Old French rompre, from Latin rumpō, rumpere (“to break”).

c: Ces vaches ont l'air de s'emmerder.

estomac.e: Inherited from Old French estomac, borrowed from Latin stomachus, from Ancient Greek στόμαχος (stómakhos).

couvrir.e: Inherited from Old French covrir, inherited from Latin cooperīre, from co- + operiō.

tâche.e: Inherited from Old French tasche, from Early Medieval Latin tasca, variant of taxa, from Latin taxō (“to handle, appraise”), from tangō (“to touch”), from Proto-Indo-European *teh₂g-, cognate with Ancient Greek τάσσω (t…
c: Cette tâche a pris trois heures.
Elle est dure à la tâche.
Ben bir koltuk rezervasyonu yaptırmak istiyorum.

brûler.e: Inherited from Middle French brusler, from Old French brusler, bruller (“to burn”), probably an enhanced form of usler (“to scorch”), from Latin ustulāre. Cognate with dialectal Italian brustolare.
c: Ce bois ne veut pas brûler.

chou.e: Inherited from Old French chous, from Latin caulis, itself akin to or derived from Ancient Greek καυλός (kaulós).
c: Il nous faut parler, mon chou.
On peut manger le chou, cru.

la fermer.e: Elliptical form of fermer sa gueule (“to shut one's mouth”)

origine.e: Borrowed from Latin orīginem (“beginning, source, birth, origin”). Replaced the older popular form orine, inherited from the same source.

poursuivre.e: Inherited from Old French porsivre, poursivre, porsuir, poursuire, porsivir, from Vulgar Latin *prosequere (attested in Vulgar or early Medieval Latin as prosevere and prosequire), from Latin prosequi.
c: Il était trop fatigué pour poursuivre.
O, daha ileri gidemeyecek kadar yorgundu.

tapis.e: Inherited from Middle French tapiz, from Vulgar Latin *tappetium, from Latin tapētem or from Byzantine Greek ταπήτιον (tapḗtion), from Ancient Greek τάπης (tápēs), from an Iranian source.

absence.e: From Latin absentia, from absēns (“absent”), present active participle of absum (“to be away or absent”), from ab (“of, by, from”) + sum (“to be”).
c: Peter est venu pendant ton absence.
Après une longue absence, il est revenu.
Uzun bir yokluktan sonra geri döndü.

tempête.e: Inherited from Old French tempeste, from Latin tempesta < tempestās.

c: Les enfants ont rempli la pièce.
Mon cœur était rempli de joie.

remplir.e: Inherited from Middle French remplir, from Old French remplir, from re- + emplir, which is itself from Vulgar Latin *implīre, from Latin implēre.

écran.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-der. Proto-Germanic *skirmiz Proto-West Germanic *skirmi Old Dutch skirm Middle Dutch schermbor.
c: Il a passé tout son temps à regarder l'écran.
Victor Hugo est un très célèbre écrivain français.
Victor Hugo çok ünlü bir Fransız yazardır.
La maison de Victor Hugo est située place des Vosges à Paris.
Victor Hugo'nun evi Paris'teki Vosges meydanındadır.
Je dois aller à un enterrement.

venger.e: Inherited from Middle French venger, vengier, from Old French vengier, from Latin vindicāre.

c: Sara a trente et un stylos.
Tu dois être en train d'inventer ça.
Ne dis pas "découvrir" quand tu veux dire "inventer".

installer.e: From Middle French, from Medieval Latin īnstallāre (“to install, put in place, establish”), from in- + stallum (“stall”), from Frankish *stall (“stall, position, place”), from Proto-Germanic *stallaz (“place, position”)…
c: Elle veut s'installer et avoir des enfants.
O yerleşmek ve çocuk sahibi olmak istiyor.

rythme.e: Learned borrowing from Latin rhythmus, itself borrowed from Ancient Greek ῥυθμός (rhuthmós).
c: Je dois trouver mon propre rythme.
Je ne peux pas suivre ton rythme.

pratique.e: Inherited from Middle French practique, from Medieval Latin prāctica.

c: Elle est venue tôt pour pratiquer.

ballon.e: Inherited from Middle French ballon. Doublet of balloune.

attirer.e: Inherited from Middle French, from Old French atirer, atirier (“to draw to oneself”), from a- + tirer (“to draw, pull out with great effort, snatch violently, tear away”), from Gothic *𐍄𐌹𐍂𐌰𐌽 (*tiran, “to tear away,…

loup.e: Inherited from Middle French loup, from an old western dialectal variant lou of Old French leu and reformed analogically from the feminine louve from Latin lupus (“wolf”).

c: O, bana bir çocuk gibi davranır.

navré.e: Past participle of navrer (“to upset, dismay”), from Middle French, from Old French navrer, nafrer (“to hurt by piercing or cutting”), from Old Norse nafra (“to pierce or bore with an auger”), from nafarr (“auger”), fro…
c: Je suis navré pour ta sœur.
Je suis navré, mais quel est votre nom déjà ?
Üzgünüm ama tekrar senin adın nedir?

proposer.e: Inherited from Old French proposer, borrowed from Latin prōpōnere, altered based on French poser.
c: Sana bir iş teklif etmek istiyorum.
Personne n'était capable de proposer une solution.

lutte.e: Inherited from Old French, from Late Latin lucta, from Latin luctor (“to wrestle”). Compare Italian lotta, Spanish lucha and Romanian luptă.

lutter.e: Inherited from Middle French luiter, from Old French luitier, from Latin luctārī.

opportunité.e: Borrowed from Latin opportūnitātem. Morphologically, from opportun + -ité.

accompagner.e: Inherited from Old French acompagner (“to associate with”), from compaing (“companion”).

c: Pourquoi te limiter à un seul ?
Neden kendinizi sadece bir taneyle sınırlıyorsunuz?

panique.e: Inherited from Middle French panique, a learned borrowing from Ancient Greek πανικός (panikós), from Πάν (Pán).

technologie.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek τεχνολογία (tekhnología, “systematic treatment (of grammar)”), from τέχνη (tékhnē, “art”) + -λογία (-logía).

briller.e: Etymology tree Proto-Dravidian *weḷ Proto-Dravidian *ūr Proto-Dravidian *weḷ-ūr Proto-Indo-Iranian *i- Proto-Indo-European *-kos Proto-Indo-Iranian *-kas Proto-Indo-Iranian *-ikas Sanskrit -इक (-ika) Prakrit -इय (-iya)…
c: Le soleil et la lune avaient commencé à briller.

afrique.e: Inherited from Old French Affrique, borrowed from Latin Āfrica.

nourrir.e: Inherited from Middle French nourrir, from Old French norrir, inherited from Latin nūtrīre.
c: Merci de nourrir le chien chaque jour.

région.e: Borrowed from Latin regiōnem. Compare the inherited Old French reiun, rëon, royon.
c: Son nom est connu de tous dans cette région.
Onun adı bu çevrede herkesçe bilinir.

salaire.e: Inherited from Old French salaire, from Latin salārium, probably a semi-learned borrowing. Cf. also the inherited Old French salier, saler (and modern salière).
c: Il gagne deux fois mon salaire.

ceinture.e: Inherited from Old French ceinture, inherited from Latin cinctūra.

profond.e: Inherited from Middle French profond, from Old French profont, relatinization of inherited parfont, parfunt, from Latin profundus.

posséder.e: From an alteration of an older Middle French possider, from Latin possidēre. Compare also the Old French forms porseoir, porseir, porsoier.
c: J'espère posséder un jour ma propre maison.
Bir gün kendi evime sahip olmayı umuyorum.
Pourquoi le gouvernement américain laisse-t-il les gens posséder des armes ?
Neden ABD hükümeti insanların silah sahibi olmalarına izin veriyor?

étonner.e: From Middle French estonner, from Old French estoner (“to be dizzy due to a violent blow”), of obscure origin.

roman.e: Borrowed from Latin romanus or derived from the French noun below, itself from Old French romanz (“common language”).
c: Ce roman est difficile à comprendre.

nana.e: Diminutive form of Anna, Anne, popularised after Émile Zola's 1880 novel Nana.

nommer.e: Inherited from Middle French nommer, from Old French nomer, from Latin nōmināre. See also nominer.
c: Je ne sais pas comment te nommer.
La petite Sophie n’était pas obéissante.

chine.e: From Persian چینی (čini, “Chinese; porcelain”), compound of چین (čin, “China”) and the suffix ـی (-i), from Middle Persian 𐭰𐭩𐭭 (čīn, “China”), ultimately from Sanskrit चीन (cīna).

technique.e: Borrowed from Ancient Greek τεχνικός (tekhnikós, “relating to art, artistic, skilful”), from τέχνη (tékhnē, “art, handicraft”).

haine.e: Inherited from Middle French haine, from Old French haine, from Frankish *hati, from Proto-Germanic *hataz. More at hate.

célibataire.e: From célibat (“celibacy”) + -aire (“-ary”). Compare Piedmontese selibatari, Occitan celibatari and Catalan celibatari.

portée.e: From feminine past participle of porter (“to carry”).
c: Ils sont à portée de voix.
Veuillez rester à portée de voix.

rouler.e: Inherited from Old French roeler (“to roll”), from Medieval Latin rotulāre, from Latin rotula.
c: Il a essayé de me rouler.
Je suis sûr que tout va rouler.

palais.e: Inherited from Middle French palays, from Old French palais, from Latin palātium. Doublet of palace.
c: Elle m'a montré le chemin au palais.
O, saraya kadar bana rehberlik yaptı.
Il m'a montré le chemin au palais.

lady.e: Borrowed from English lady, from Middle English lady, from Old English hlǣfdīġe.

jeudi.e: Inherited from Old French jeudi, jusdi, from Latin Jovis diēs or Iovis diēs, variant of diēs Iovis (“day of Jupiter”).

circonstance.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *(s)ker-der. Ancient Greek κίρκος (kírkos)bor.

canapé.e: From Old French conopé, conope (later altered in form and meaning based on Medieval Latin canāpēum, alteration of canōpēum (“mosquito net”)), itself from Latin cōnōpēum (“seat with a canopy”), from Ancient Greek κωνωπεῖ…
c: Ce canapé prend trop de place.

affronter.e: Inherited from Old French afronter (“to face; to confront; to slap in the face”), either a French derivation a- + front + -er, or an inheritance from an unattested Vulgar Latin *affrontāre (“to strike against”), from La…

c: Si on veut connaitre un pays, il faut apprendre son histoire.
Bir ulusu bilmek istiyorsan onun tarihini öğrenmelisin.

élève.e: Deverbal from élever (“to raise, bring up, elevate”).

pêche.e: Inherited from Middle French pesche, from Old French pesche, from Vulgar Latin *pessica (cf. Medieval Latin pesca), from Late Latin persica, from Latin persicum. Doublet of persique.

masque.e: Etymology tree Late Latin mascara Latin *mascra Proto-Indo-European *mesg-der. Proto-Germanic *maskwǭ Proto-West Germanic *maskābor. Latin masca Italian mascherabor. French masque Borrowed from Italian maschera.

masquer.e: Etymology tree Late Latin mascara Latin *mascra Proto-Indo-European *mesg-der. Proto-Germanic *maskwǭ Proto-West Germanic *maskābor. Latin masca Italian mascherabor. French masque Proto-Italic *-āzi ▲ Latin -ereinflu.
c: Le monde est un grand bal où chacun est masqué.
Dünya herkesin bir maske taktığı büyük bir balo.

couvert.e: Inherited from Old French covert, from Latin coopertus.

malheur.e: Inherited from Middle French mal-heur; univerbation of mal + heur, literally “mishap, misfortune”.
c: À toute chose malheur est bon.
Ça porte malheur de dire ça.

royaume.e: Inherited from Old French reaume, realme, a derivative of real, or from an alteration (with influence from royal) of Old French reiame, from Latin regimine. Compare régime.
c: Elle était la plus belle femme du royaume.
O tüm krallıktaki en güzel kadındı.

porc.e: Inherited from Middle French porc, from Old French porc, from Latin porcus, from Proto-Italic *porkos, from Proto-Indo-European *pórḱos (“young swine, young pig”).

vingt.e: Inherited from Middle French vingt, from Old French vint, from Latin vīgintī, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁wih₁ḱm̥ti, *dwi(h₁)dḱm̥ti.
c: Il gagne vingt dollars par jour.

gêne.e: Inherited from Middle French gehenne (spelling influenced by géhenne), from Old French gehine (“punishment resulting from admission of guilt”), from gehir, geïr (“to admit, confess, acknowledge”), from Frankish *jehhjan…
c: Le bruit ne nous gêne pas.
Ça te gêne d'être vue avec moi ?

gêner.e: Inherited from Middle French genner, from Old French gehisner, derivative of gehine (“torture resulting from confession, embarrassment”), of Frankish origin. By surface analysis, gêne + -er.

bloc.e: Inherited from Middle French bloc (“a considerable piece of something heavy, block”), from Old French bloc (“log, block”), from Middle Dutch blok (“treetrunk”), from Old Dutch *blok (“log”), from Frankish or Proto-West…
c: J'ai écrit le numéro de téléphone sur le bloc-notes.
Il a démarré un nouveau business.

alarme.e: Borrowed from Italian all'arme (“to arms”), with univerbation. Compare alerte.

c: Tom a eu un rencard avec Marie.
Tom Mary ile bir randevuya gitti.
Je veux me concentrer sur ça.

singe.e: Inherited from Middle French singe, from Old French singe, inherited from Latin sīmius.
c: Son ami ressemble à un singe.
Onun erkek arkadaşı bir maymuna benziyor.

colle.e: Inherited from Vulgar Latin colla, from Ancient Greek κόλλα (kólla, “glue”). Compare Italian colla, Portuguese and Spanish cola.

c: J'ai essayé de lui en coller une.

central.e: Borrowed from Latin centrālis. By surface analysis, centre + -al.
c: Il joue un rôle important, presque central.
O önemli, neredeyse kilit rol oynamaktadır.
Cette maison n'a pas de chauffage central.

naturel.e: Inherited from Middle French naturel, from Old French natural, a borrowing from Latin nātūrālis. By surface analysis, nature + -el.

étape.e: From Middle French estappe, from Old French estaple, from Middle Dutch stapel, from Old Dutch stapul, from Frankish *stapul.

cage.e: Inherited from Old French cage, from Latin cavea. This form did not undergo the palatalization of c before a.

davantage.e: From Middle French davantaige, from Old French d'avantage, corresponding to de + avantage.

c: Pourquoi ne portes-tu pas ton alliance ?
Il y a une alliance importante entre ces deux pays.
Bu iki ülke arasında önemli bir ittifak vardır.

collier.e: Inherited from Middle French collier, from Old French colier, a variant (deriving from Late Latin collārium) of coler, from Late Latin collāre.

c: Bonjour, mon petit rayon de soleil.

gâcher.e: Inherited from Middle French gascher (“to waste, ruin; row (with oars)”), from Old French gaschier, gacher, gasser (“to soil, spoil, waste”) and Old French gaschier, guaschier, waschier (“to wash, soak”), both from Old…

c: Quant aux chiens, je les aime.
Quant à moi, je veux rester dehors.
Ils complotent pour assassiner le roi.
Ils ont tenté d'assassiner le président.

placard.e: Etymology tree Old French plaquer Old French placard French placard Inherited from Old French derivative of plaquer (“to stick, to affix”). By surface analysis, plaque + -ard.

soif.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- Proto-Indo-European *-éyti Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰéyti Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰey- Proto-Indo-European *-tis Proto-Indo-European *dʰgʷʰéytis Latin sitis Old French seif O…

condition.e: From Middle French condition, from Old French condicion, borrowed from Latin condiciōnem.

miel.e: Inherited from Middle French miel, from Old French miel, Vulgar Latin *melem m or f, from Latin mel n.
c: Elle est douce comme le miel.

créature.e: Borrowed from Late Latin creatūra (like English creature), from creo, creare (“to create”).
c: Sans air, aucune créature ne pourrait vivre.
Sans eau, aucune créature ne pourrait vivre.
Il a été payé au black.
Il travaille au black comme stripteaseur.
O, bir striptizci olarak ek işte çalışıyor.

kilomètre.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰes- Proto-Indo-European *-lom Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰesliyoy Proto-Hellenic *kʰehliyoi Ancient Greek χίλιοι (khílioi)der.
c: Il y a mille mètres dans un kilomètre.
Combien y a-t-il de mètres dans un kilomètre ?
Bir kilometrede kaç tane metre var?
Je me suis associé à lui.

monnaie.e: Inherited from Old French moneie, monoie, from Latin monēta. Cognate with English money, Spanish moneda, Portuguese moeda, Italian moneta.

moquer.e: From Middle French mocquer, from Old French moquer, from Middle Dutch mocken (“to mumble”) or Middle Low German mucken (“to grumble, speak with half-opened mouth”), both from Old Saxon *mokkian, *mukkian (“to low, mumbl…
c: Arrête de te moquer de moi !
Tom ne devrait pas se moquer de Mary.
Tom'un Mary ile alay etmemesi gerek.

clinique.e: From the Late Latin clīnicus (“a bed-ridden person”, “one baptized on a sick-bed”, “a physician”).
c: Hier, j'ai amené mon chat à la clinique vétérinaire.
Je fais appel à vous pour contribuer à la nouvelle clinique.
Yeni kliniğe katkıda bulunmanı rica ediyorum.
Tape aussi fort que tu peux.
Elinden geldiği kadar sert tekme vur.

taper.e: Inherited from Middle French taper, from Old French tapper, taper (“to tap”), of Germanic origin, from Frankish *tappōn, *dabbōn (“to strike”) or from Middle Low German tappen, tapen (“to tap, rap, strike”).
c: Je peux taper 50 mots par minute.

classique.e: Learned borrowing from Latin classicus (“relating to the classes of Roman citizenry, especially the highest”), from classis (“class”). Doublet of clasico.

temple.e: Inherited from Old French temple, borrowed from Latin templum.
c: Je ne vois pas de temple.
Il y avait ici un vieux temple.
Cette société a vendu des produits dangereux.

passion.e: Inherited from Middle French passion, from Old French passion, borrowed from Latin passiōnem, ultimately from patior. Cognate with patience.

existence.e: Inherited from Old French existence, from Late Latin existentia (“existence”).

c: Au plaisir de correspondre avec vous.
Analyser ces données nous prendra pas mal de temps.
Bu verileri analiz etmemiz biraz zaman alacak.
Cela a pris beaucoup de temps pour analyser les données.
Verileri analiz etmek uzun zaman aldı.

mystère.e: Inherited from Middle French mystere, a borrowing from Latin mystērium, itself borrowed from Ancient Greek μῠστήρῐον (mŭstḗrĭon). See also métier.

port.e: Inherited from Old French port, borrowed from Latin portus, from Proto-Italic *portus, from Proto-Indo-European *pértus (“crossing”), from *per- (“to go forth, to cross”).
c: Le bateau est maintenant au port.
Elles ont probablement vu notre bateau arriver au port.

tension.e: Inherited from Middle French tension, borrowed from Latin tensiō.
c: On pouvait sentir la tension dans l'air.

qualité.e: From Old French, from Latin qualitātem.
c: Ce magasin offre un service de qualité.
La qualité de ton anglais est incroyable.
C'est une question de sécurité nationale.

national.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁- Proto-Indo-European *-tis Proto-Indo-European *ǵénh₁tisder. Proto-Italic *gnātiō Latin nātiōbor.
c: Il est devenu un héros national.
Tom est devenu un héros national.

vierge.e: Inherited from Middle French verge, from Old French verge, vierge, virge, from a shortening of virgene, from Latin virgō, according to the Trésor de la Langue Française etymological dictionary, a borrowing.

piano.e: Borrowed from Italian piano. Doublet of plain and plan.

c: Comment trouvez-vous le secteur du Contrôle de qualité ?
Benim bir sürü ev ödevim var.

pot.e: Inherited from Middle French pot, from Old French pot (“pot”), from Vulgar Latin pottum, pottus (“pot, jar”), from Frankish *pott, from Proto-Germanic *puttaz (“pot, jar, tub”), from Proto-Indo-European *budn- (“a kind…

cigarette.e: Etymology tree Latin cicādader. Vulgar Latin *cicār(r)a Spanish cigarra? Spanish cigarrobor. French cigare Proto-Indo-European *-tós Proto-Italic *-tosder.?

c: Ça a bien meilleur goût que ce que je bouffe d'habitude.
Bu genellikle yediğimizden çok daha iyi tat veriyor.

bouffer.e: Inherited from Old French bouffer, originally "to puff up," from Medieval Latin buffa, itself echoic of puffing out cheeks.
c: On a bouffé de la pizza et du poulet au déjeuner.
Öğle yemeği saatinde domuz gibi pizza ve tavuk yedik.

jugement.e: Inherited from Old French jugement. By surface analysis, juger + -ment. Or from Late Latin iūdicāmentum, from Latin iūdicō (“to pass judgement upon”).

courageux.e: From Old French corageus, corresponding to courage + -eux.

bibliothèque.e: Inherited from Middle French bibliotheque, borrowed from Latin bibliothēca (“library”), originally from Ancient Greek βιβλιοθήκη (bibliothḗkē, “book-room”). Morphologically biblio- + -thèque.

c: Son désir est d'aller en Amérique.

saler.e: Inherited from Old French, from a Vulgar Latin root *salāre, from a change in conjugation of Latin salīre (“to salt”), from sal. Compare Italian salare, Romanian săra, Spanish, Portuguese, and Catalan salar.

courrier.e: Etymology tree Italian correre Italian -iere Italian corrierebor. Middle French corier French courrier From Middle French corier, a borrowing of Italian corriere. Compare Medieval Latin currerius.

merveilleuse.e: Noun use of feminine form of merveilleux ‘marvellous’.

fumée.e: Feminine past participle of the verb fumer; from Middle French fumée, fumee, from Old French fumee. Replaced Old French fum.

tasse.e: ), from Arabic طَاس (ṭās) (a shortening of طَسْت (ṭast)), from Middle Persian tšt' (tašt), ultimately from the past participle of the Proto-Iranian verb *taš- (“to make, construct; to cut”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *tā́…

hall.e: Borrowed from English hall. Doublet of halle.
c: Ce hall était plein de monde.

pile.e: Inherited from Old French, from Latin pīla (through Italian pila for the “battery” sense). The “tail of a coin” sense is probably derived from previous senses, but it's not known for sure.

c: C'est difficile de soigner un bébé qui pleure.
Cette règle ne s'applique pas aux urgences.
Bu kural acil durumlarda geçerli değildir.
Veux-tu me garder mes effets de valeur, s'il te plait ?
Benim için eşyalarıma göz kulak olur musun lütfen?

essai.e: Inherited from Middle French, from Old French essai, from Late Latin exagium (“weighing”), hence English assay (compare also Spanish ensayo), from Latin exigō; the original sense of "trial" (if the gold is good) drifted…

fruit.e: Inherited from Middle French fruict, a Latinized spelling of Old French fruit, from Latin fruitus (“enjoyment, proceeds, profits, produce, income”), frūctus, a derivative of fruor (“have the benefit of, to use, to enjoy…

c: Les taux d'intérêt ont fait du yo-yo toute l'année.
Faiz oranları bütün yıl aşağı yukarı oynatıldı.

charlotte.e: From the female forename Charlotte, or from Old French char laitée (“meat with milk”): char (“meat”) + laitée (“milk”).

risqué.e: The adjective is derived from the past participle of risquer (“to put at risk; to risk”).

avouer.e: Inherited from Old French avoer, from Latin advocāre. The modern form is expected as in louer (from locāre).
c: Tom'u itiraf etmesi için ikna etmelisin.
Cette fenêtre est à l'épreuve des balles.

conduite.e: Inherited from Latin conducta < conductus. Compare Italian condotta.

c: Démontrez que P est un ensemble partiellement ordonné.
Est-ce que Robin des Bois est vivant ?

avantage.e: From Old French avantage. Derivable from avant + -age.

retenir.e: Inherited from Middle French retenir, from Old French retenir, from Vulgar Latin *retenīre, from Latin retinēre, from re- + teneō (“to hold”).

lover.e: A 17th century borrowing from North Sea Germanic language verb "lofen, lufen".

miroir.e: Inherited from Middle French miroir m, Old French mireor m. Equivalent to mirer + -oir.

jaune.e: Etymology tree Latin galbinus Old French jaune Middle French jaune French jaune Inherited from Middle French jaune, iaune, from Old French jaune, jalne, from Latin galbinus.

effort.e: Inherited from Middle French, from Old French esfort, from esforcier; morphologically, deverbal from efforcer. Compare Spanish esfuerzo, Catalan esforç, Portuguese esforço, Italian sforzo.

crie.e: cri + -e; clipping of Christenaux (now "Knistenaux"), from Cree Kenisteniwuik (the name of a Cree village)

disque.e: Borrowed from Latin discus. Doublet of dais, which was inherited from Old French deis, dois.
c: Mon disque dur est presque plein.
Çağrıyı iptal etmeme gerek var mı?
C'est le chef de notre section.

catherine.e: From Medieval Latin Katerīna, from Latin Ecaterīna, from Ancient Greek Αἰκατερίνη (Aikaterínē), *Ἑκατερίνη (*Hekaterínē).

aube.e: Inherited from Old French albe, from Vulgar Latin *alba, from Latin albus (“white”).

précis.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *per- Proto-Indo-European *preh₂- Proto-Indo-European *-i Proto-Indo-European *préh₂i?

vampire.e: Borrowed from German Vampir, from Serbo-Croatian vampir.

échec.e: Inherited from Old French eschec, from Medieval Latin scaccus, from Arabic شَاه (šāh, “king or check at chess, shah”), from Classical Persian شاه (šāh, “king”), from Middle Persian 𐭬𐭫𐭪𐭠 (mlkʾ /⁠šāh⁠/), from Old Pers…

mexique.e: Borrowed from Spanish México, from Classical Nahuatl Mēxihco.
c: Elle est allée seule au Mexique.

figure.e: Inherited from Old French figure, borrowed from Latin figūra.
c: Cet endroit ne figure pas sur la carte.

urgent.e: Borrowed from Late Latin urgentem, present participle of urgeō.

médical.e: Borrowed from Medieval Latin medicālis (compare Classical Latin medicīnālis, whence the French médicinal), from Latin medicus.
c: As-tu vu le dossier médical de Tom ?

chiffre.e: From Medieval Latin cifra (“zero”), from Andalusian Arabic صِفر (ṣifr, “empty”). Doublet of zéro.

c: Elle passe carrément trop de temps à naviguer sur la toile.
O, internette sörf yaparak çok fazla zaman harcar.

pointer.e: From point + -er, from the past participle of poindre.
c: N'oublie pas de pointer avant de quitter le travail.
İşten ayrılmadan önce kart basmayı unutma.
Tu n'as pas envie de pointer cette arme vers moi.

interroger.e: Borrowed from Latin interrogāre. Doublet of entraver.
c: Ils sont en train de l'interroger.

sauce.e: Inherited from Old French sause, from Vulgar Latin *salsa, nominal use of the feminine of Latin salsus (“salted”), perfect participle of saliō (“to salt”), from sāl.
c: Vous voulez un peu plus de sauce ?
J'aimerais avoir la sauce sur le côté, s'il vous plaît.

séance.e: From séant + -ance, possibly corresponding to Latin sedentia.
c: Je me sens bien après une séance de gym.

allier.e: Inherited from Old French alier, from Latin alligāre. Doublet of the form aloyer, from the Old French variant aloiier.
c: Il faut que vous y alliez.
La famille Johnson adore faire la fête.
La chambre de M. Johnson était une grande chambre.

foot.e: Clipping of football; pseudo-anglicism. Doublet of pied.

c: O yapmak için çok ciddi bir suçlama.

bagage.e: Either from Late Latin *baga (“a vessel type”), or from Old French bague (“pack, bundle”); ultimately from the North Germanic/Scandinavian source (Old Norse baggi) that yielded English bag.

boule.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *bew-der.? Proto-Indo-European *bʰel-der.? Latin bullader.? Frankish *bollāder.?

nu.e: Inherited from Middle French nu, from Old French nu, from Latin nūdus, from Proto-Indo-European *nogʷós.

patience.e: Inherited from Middle French patience, from Old French pacience (modern English patience), from Latin patientia (“suffering; endurance, patience”), from patiens, present active participle of patior (“suffer, experience,…

poissons.e: the plural of poisson (“fish”), from Latin piscis (plural pisces, hence Pisces); the municipality (and hence the canton) may have an entirely different (Latin?
c: Il y a six poissons dans la boîte.
Teneke kutu içinde altı tane balık var.

égal.e: Inherited from Old French egal, igal, a semi-learned borrowing from Latin aequālis, displacing inherited Old French evel, ivel, oel, uel.

organiser.e: From Middle French organiser, borrowed from Medieval Latin organizāre.

œuvre.e: Inherited from Old French uevre, inherited from Latin opera. Doublet of opéra and opus.

c: Elle est membre de cette organisation.
Je suis le porte-parole de cette organisation.

texas.e: Borrowed from English Texas, from Spanish Texas, Tejas.
c: Il parlait avec une voix traînante typique du Texas.
O tipik bir Teksaslı şivesi ile konuştu.
Il a quitté la capitale mexicaine pour retourner au Texas.
O Texas'a dönmek için Meksika başkentinden ayrıldı.

attitude.e: Borrowed from Italian attitudine (“attitude, aptness”), from Medieval Latin aptitūdō (“aptitude”) (whence French aptitude) and actitūdō (“acting, posture”).

c: Je t'ai dit de signer le document.
Pouvez-vous signer ce document s'il vous plaît ?
Je suis enchantée de te rencontrer.

proposition.e: From Latin prōpositiōnem (“statement, proposition”), from prōpōnō (“propose”), from pōnō (“place; assume”).

serpent.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *serp- Proto-Indo-European *sérpeti Proto-Italic *serpō Latin serpō Latin serpēns Old French serpent Middle French serpent French serpent Inherited from Middle French serpent, from Old…

audience.e: Inherited from Old French audience, borrowed from Latin audientia, from present participle audiēns (“hearing”), from verb audiō (“to hear”).
c: Quand le juge parle, toute la salle d'audience l'écoute.
Hakim konuştuğunda, mahkeme salonundaki herkes dinler.

télévision.e: From télé- (“far off”) + vision (“seeing”), first used by Constantin Perskyi in a paper ("Télévision au moyen de l’électricité") read to the International Electricity Congress at the International World Fair in Paris on…

patte.e: From Middle French, from Old French pade, pate (“paw, foot of an animal”), from Vulgar Latin *patta (“paw, foot”), borrowed from Frankish *patta (“paw, sole of the foot”), from Proto-Germanic *pat-, *paþa- (“to walk, tr…

possibilité.e: Inherited from Old French possibilité, borrowed from Latin possibilitātem.

poison.e: From Old French poison f, inherited from Latin pōtiōnem f. Doublet of potion f, a borrowing. Cognate with English poison, potion.

maudit.e: From maudire, from Old French maudire, maldire, from Latin maledīcō. Equivalent to mal + dit.
c: Elle le maudit pour avoir oublié sa promesse.

cochon.e: Originally imitative of the noise a pig makes.

paire.e: Inherited from Old French paire, from Latin paria, neuter plural of pār.

c: Elle travaille comme jeune-fille au pair.
O bir au pair olarak çalışır.
Tom ne semble tout simplement pas pouvoir aller de pair avec Mary.
Tom sadece Mary ile iyi geçiniyor gibi görünemiyor.

condamner.e: Inherited from Old French condamner, borrowed from Latin condemnāre.
c: Ne condamne pas si tu ne veux pas être condamné.

sauvage.e: Inherited from Old French sauvage, salvage, from Vulgar Latin salvāticus, from Latin silvāticus, from silva (“forest”).

domaine.e: Inherited from Old French domaine, demaine, from Latin dominium or dominicus.

poussière.e: Inherited from Old French pousiere, derived from pous, from Vulgar Latin *pulvus, neuter form derived from Latin pulvis m.
c: Enlève la poussière de tes chaussures.

rat.e: Inherited from Middle French rat (“rat”), from Old French rat (“rat”); ultimately of Germanic origin, from Old High German rato (“rat”) or Frankish *rato (“rat”).
c: Mon chat a tué ce rat.
Le rat est là ! Allez chercher le chat !
Fare burada! Git de kediyi çağır!

ajouter.e: Inherited from Old French ajoster, from Vulgar Latin *adiuxtāre, *adjuxtāre, from Latin ad + iuxta. Compare also ajuster.

séparer.e: Borrowed from Latin sēparāre. Doublet of sevrer, which was inherited.
c: Personne ne peut désormais nous séparer.

valise.e: Inherited from Middle French valise, from Medieval Latin valesia, valixia, from Late Latin valisia, possibly from Gaulish *valisia (“leather bag”), from Proto-Celtic *val- (“to enclose, surround”), from Proto-Indo-Europ…

idéal.e: From Late Latin ideālis (“existing in idea”), from Ancient Greek ἰδέᾱ (idéā, “idea”).

empereur.e: From Middle French empereur, from Old French empereor, from Latin imperātōrem.
c: Je suis désolé, mais je ne veux pas être empereur.
Üzgünüm ama bir imparator olmak istiyorum.
La princesse implora le pardon de l'empereur.

vincent.e: Derived from Latin Vincentius, from vincēns.

printemps.e: Inherited from Old French printans, from prime tans (“first time, first season”), from Latin prīmum tempus. Displaced Latin vēr.

bonbon.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dewh₂-der.? Proto-Italic *dwenos Archaic Latin duenos Old Latin duonus Latin bonus Old French bon Middle French bon French bonredup. French bonbon Reduplication of bon (“good”).

légende.e: From Old French legende, from Medieval Latin legenda, feminine of Latin legendus, gerundive of legēre.
c: Mets une légende sur cette photo.
Ona benim için bir öpücük ver.
C'est une espèce en voie de disparition.
La police est en train d'enquêter sur sa disparition.

poule.e: Inherited from Old French, from Vulgar Latin pulla, feminine form of Latin pullus.

éducation.e: Learned borrowing from Latin ēducātiō. By surface analysis, éduquer + -ation.

dragon.e: Inherited from Old French dragon, perhaps borrowed from Old Occitan dragon, from Latin dracō, from Ancient Greek δράκων (drákōn). Doublet of drac.

plaque.e: From Middle Dutch placken (“to patch, beat metal into a thin plate”), from placke (“disk, patch, stain”), from *Old Dutch plagga (“patch”), from Proto-Germanic *plaggą (“patch”).
c: J'ai mis la plaque à ton nom.
Tom vient de se faire plaquer.

auparavant.e: Inherited from Middle French auparavant, a univerbation of au + par + avant.

mobile.e: Learned borrowing from Latin mōbilis. Doublet of meuble.

musée.e: From Latin mūsēum (“library, study”), from Ancient Greek Μουσεῖον (Mouseîon), shrine of the Muses (Μοῦσα (Moûsa)).

c: Je porte mes bijoux en argent.

bijou.e: Borrowed from Breton bizoù, bizou (“ring”), from biz (“finger”).

c: Avez-vous déjà eu un traitement psychologique ?
Önceden psikolojik bir tedavi gördünüz mü?

sable.e: Inherited from Old French, from Vulgar Latin sablum, from Latin sabulum, alternative form of sabulō. Compare sablon, which was used more often in Old French. Compare Italian sabbia, Occitan sabla.

balance.e: Inherited from Middle French balance, from Old French balance, from Vulgar Latin *bilancia, from Latin bilanx, from bi- (see Latin bis) and lanx.

c: Ne fais pas balancer le bateau !
Je ne vais pas te balancer aux flics.

critique.e: Learned borrowing from Latin criticus, from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós).

fièvre.e: Inherited from Middle French fievre, from Old French fievre, from Latin febris.

raisonnable.e: Inherited from Old French resnable, from Late Latin ratiōnābilis, from Latin ratiō. Equivalent to raison + -able.

déposer.e: Borrowed from Latin dēpōnere (“to put aside or away”), influenced by poser; equivalent of French dé- + poser.

imagination.e: Inherited from Middle French, from Old French imaginacion, borrowed from Latin imāginātiōnem.

chirurgie.e: Borrowed from Latin chirurgia, from chirurgus, from Ancient Greek χειρουργός (kheirourgós).
c: La chirurgie est la meilleure solution.

ordinaire.e: Inherited from Old French ordinaire, borrowed from Latin ōrdinārius, from Latin ōrdō (whence French ordre) + -ārius (whence -aire).

c: Hollywood n'est plus ce qu'il était.
Mon rêve est de devenir acteur à Hollywood.
Hayalim Holivud'da bir aktör olarak başarılı olmaktır.

magazine.e: From English magazine. Doublet of magasin.

matière.e: From Old French matiere, borrowed from Latin materia.
c: Qui est responsable, en cette matière ?
Quand avez-vous eu votre dernier rapport sexuel ?
En son ne zaman cinsel ilişkiye girdiniz?
Je veux avoir une relation sexuelle avec elle.

bagarre.e: Uncertain. Compare Middle French bagarot (“noise, tumult, contention, strife”) and Provençal bagarro (“brawl”), possibly from Basque batzarre (“meeting, assembly”). Compare also Old Norse bágr (“resistance, struggle”).

solide.e: Borrowed from Latin solidus. Doublet of sou.

c: Je ne lui suis pas lié.
Je ne suis lié à ce crime en aucune manière.
Ben herhangi bir şekilde bu suçla bağlantılı değilim.

lier.e: Inherited from Old French lier, from Latin ligāre, from Proto-Indo-European *leyǵ- (“to bind”).

cercle.e: Inherited from Old French cercle, from Latin circulus.

caroline.e: From Italian Carolina or its etymon Latin Carolīna.
c: Tom habite en Caroline du Nord.
Joe et Caroline s'occupent de notre chien.
Je n'ai jamais été au cirque.

amen.e: Borrowed from Ecclesiastical Latin āmēn, from Ancient Greek ἀμήν (amḗn), from Biblical Hebrew אָמֵן (ʾāmēn, “certainly, truly”).

congé.e: Inherited from Old French congié, cungié, cunged, congiet, cumgiet, from Latin commeātus. As an architectural term, a calque of Ancient Greek ἀποφυγή (apophugḗ, “a leave, an escape; an architectural feature”).
c: Demain est mon jour de congé.
Demain est son jour de congé.

roy.e: Inherited from Old French roy (literally “king, ruler”). Doublet of roi.
c: Elle a joué aux cartes avec Roy.
Je n'ai jamais entendu Roy chanter une chanson en public.
Roy'un herkesin içinde bir şarkı söylediğini hiç duymadım.

beurre.e: ), from a regional (eastern or western) variant of burre, from Old French burre, bure, from Latin būtȳrum, from Ancient Greek βούτῡρον (boútūron, “butter”, literally “cow-cheese”).

émotion.e: From émouvoir + -tion, using the formation of motion as an antecedent.

stade.e: From Latin stadium, from Ancient Greek στάδιον (stádion), neuter form of στάδιος (stádios, “stable, firm”), from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to be standing”).

entraîner.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₁én Proto-Italic *en Proto-Italic *en- Latin in- Old French en- French en- Proto-Indo-European *dʰregʰ-der.?

allemand.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *h₂el-der.? Proto-Indo-European *h₂elnós Proto-Germanic *allaz Proto-Germanic *ala- Proto-Indo-European *mon- Proto-Germanic *mann- Proto-Germanic *alamann-bor.

blond.e: From Medieval Latin blondus, of Germanic origin: probably from Frankish *blund (“a mixed color between golden and light-brown”), from Proto-Germanic *blundaz (“mixed, blinding”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰl…
c: Bu uzun boylu sarışın adam kim?

japon.e: Etymology tree Hokkien 日本 (Ji̍t-pún)bor. Malay Jepangbor. Portuguese Japãobor. French Japon Borrowed from Portuguese Japão.
c: J'aimerais bien pouvoir aller au Japon.

malheureux.e: From mal- + heureux. Cognate with Piedmontese maleureus, maleuros.

barbara.e: From Latin Barbara (name of a legendary saint), feminine form of barbarus, from Ancient Greek βάρβαρος (bárbaros, “strange, foreign”).
c: Comment s'est débrouillée Barbara lors de son passage du permis hier ?
Dün Barbara'nın sürücü testi nasıl geçti?
Le succès de Barbara ne saurait être remis en question.

épaule.e: Inherited from Middle French espaule, from Old French espalle, from Vulgar Latin *spatla, from Late Latin spathula (“flat, broad piece”), itself the diminutive of Latin spatha (“straight sword”) (whence French épée (“sw…

c: D'accord, je pense que j'ai pigé.

piger.e: Believed to be derived from an adjective meaning "caught", from Late Latin *pedicus, from Latin pedica (“snare, shackle, fetter”), and therefore doublet of piéger.

taux.e: Inherited from Old French tauxer, variant of taxer (“to tax”).
c: Quel est le taux de change ?
Quel est le taux de change du jour ?
Ce n'est pas ma mamie mais ma maman.
O benim büyükannem değil; o benim annem.
Le but du voyage, c'était de rendre visite à mamie.
À quoi tu penses en voyant cette image ?

orange.e: Inherited from Middle French orange, from Old French orenge, short form of late pomme d'orenge or pomme d'orange, which was calqued after Old Italian melarancia (mela + arancia).

ouverture.e: Inherited from Old French overture, from Vulgar Latin *opertūra, from Latin apertūra. Doublet of aperture, a borrowing. Compare Catalan obertura.
c: Dan fut tué deux jours avant l'ouverture du procès.
Dan, deney başlamadan henüz iki gün önce öldürüldü.
Tu devrais faire preuve de plus d'ouverture d'esprit.

huile.e: Inherited from Middle French huyle, from Old French oile, from Latin oleum, from olea (“olive”), from Ancient Greek ἐλαία (elaía, “olive”).

sire.e: Inherited from Old French sire (nominative form), from Vulgar Latin *seior (used as a term of address), a contracted form of Latin senior (compare French seigneur, derived from the accusative form), perhaps influenced b…

parfum.e: Inherited from Middle French parfum, from parfumer (“to scent”), borrowed from Old Occitan perfumar or another language around the Mediterranean coast, cf.

cap.e: Borrowed from Occitan cap, from Latin caput. Doublet of chef.

c: Je ne suis pas une sainte.

camarade.e: From Spanish camarada, itself from cámara (“chamber”) rather than Italian camerata which is slightly later but which influenced the form camerade which is attested in the 16th and 17th centuries.
c: Je connais ta camarade de chambre.
Je suis désolé, mon père est éliminé.
Ils ont éliminé toutes les imperfections.

croix.e: Inherited from Middle French croix, from Old French croix, crois, from the Latin crucem. Doublet of crux, croiseur, and cruiser.
c: Je vois une croix en bois.

large.e: Inherited from Middle French large, from Old French large, from Latin largus, larga, largum (“abundant, plentiful, copious, large, much”).

moral.e: Inherited from Middle French moral, from Old French moral, borrowed from Latin morālis.
c: O iyi bir ruh hali içerisindeydi.
Le moral de ces hommes était excellent.
Monsieur Wilson est fier de sa maison.
M. Wilson est en colère contre Dennis.

thérapie.e: Learned borrowing from Ancient Greek θεραπεία (therapeía).

c: Il a décidé de quitter la troupe.
Cette actrice est l'étoile rayonnante de la troupe.

signature.e: From signer + -ture; cf. Medieval Latin signatura.

c: Madame Parker le salua avec un sourire.
Bayan Parker bir gülümseme ile onu selamladı.
M. Parker tenta de manger avec des baguettes.

éloigner.e: Inherited from Middle French esloigner, from Old French esloignier, itself probably from loing, or alternatively from Vulgar Latin *exlongāre, from Latin longe.
c: Pouvez-vous vous éloigner, s'il vous plaît ?

trahir.e: Inherited from Middle French trahir < Old French traïr, itself from Latin trādō 'betray'.
c: Je ne vais pas te trahir.
Tu ne devrais pas trahir ta parole.

enterrer.e: Inherited from Middle French enterrer, from Old French enterrer, from Vulgar Latin *interrāre (“to put into earth”), from Latin terra. Equivalent to en- (“into”) + terre (“earth”) + -er (infinitive marker).
c: On ne peut pas enterrer la vérité.
Le chien était occupé à enterrer son os dans le jardin.

adaptation.e: Borrowed from Medieval Latin adaptātiōnem, from Latin adaptō (“to fit, adjust, modify; to adapt, fit or adjust to”).
c: L'adaptation est la clé pour survivre.

brave.e: Probably borrowed from Italian bravo. Compare Spanish, Portuguese bravo. Doublet of bravo.

jeunesse.e: From jeune + -esse; found in Old French as juenesce. Less likely from a Vulgar Latin *juvenitia. Compare Italian giovinezza.
c: Cette chanson me rappelle ma jeunesse.
C'était une beauté dans sa jeunesse.

guérir.e: Inherited from Middle French guérir, guerir, garir, from Old French garir, guarir (“to guarantee, protect, give health to”), from Frankish *warjan (“to defend, protect”), from Proto-Germanic *warjaną (“to defend, guard”…

c: Les machines à écrire font beaucoup de bruit.
Peu de gens ont des machines à écrire.
Les Polonaises ne voulaient pas que Justin Bieber vienne en Pologne.
Polonyalı kızlar, Justin Bieber'ın Polonya'ya gelmesini istemediler.

sommet.e: Inherited from Old French somet, sommette, diminutive derivation of som (“highest part, top of a hill”) from Latin summum.
c: L'art était alors à son sommet.
La vue du sommet est très jolie.

géant.e: Inherited from Old French gaiant, jaiant, jaianz, from Vulgar Latin *gagantem, through assimilation from Latin gigantem, from Ancient Greek γίγας (gígas, “giant”).
c: Le géant n'était aimé de personne.
Dan et Linda ont des problèmes.
Tom est tombé amoureux de Linda.

territoire.e: Borrowed from Latin territōrium. Compare the inherited doublet terroir.

portefeuille.e: Etymology tree French porte Proto-Indo-European *bʰleh₃-der. Proto-Indo-European *bʰolh₃yom? Proto-Indo-European *dʰelh₁-der. Proto-Indo-European *dʰolh₁yom?

scénario.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *(s)ḱeh₃-der. Ancient Greek σκηνή (skēnḗ)bor. Latin scēnabor. Italian scena Proto-Indo-European *-yósder. Proto-Italic *-āzios Latin -āriusnom. Latin -āriumbor.

emprunter.e: Inherited from Middle French emprunter, from Old French emprunter, from Early Medieval Latin imprūntāre, from Vulgar Latin *imprūmūtāre, modified from Early Medieval Latin imprōmūtuāre.

tours.e: From Latin Turonum, from Turones, the name of the area's Gaulish inhabitants in antiquity.
c: Arrête de me jouer des tours !
Elle me joue souvent des tours.

tentative.e: Borrowed from Medieval Latin tentātīva, from tentō (“to attempt”).
c: C'est bien, pour une première tentative.

décès.e: Inherited from Middle French deces, from Old French deces, from Latin dēcessus, past participle of dēcēdō (“depart, die”).
c: Quelle était la cause du décès ?
Dix ans ont passé depuis son décès.
Onun ölümünden beri on yıl geçti.
Lord Carnarvon était un égyptologue amateur.
Lord Carnarvon amatör bir Eski Mısır bilimcisiydi.
Lord Carnarvon finança les fouilles de la tombe de Toutânkhamon.
Lord Carnarvon, Tutankhamun'un mezarının kazısını finanse etti.
Monsieur Davis a l'air très fatigué.
Sammy Davis était un chanteur excellent.

supérieur.e: Inherited from Old French superior, borrowed from Latin superior.

précieux.e: First attested in Old French as precïus. Borrowed from Latin pretiōsus (“precious, of great value”).

poil.e: From an earlier Old French peil, from Latin pilus, from Proto-Indo-European *pil-.

c: Elles se cachèrent dans la cave.

objectif.e: Learned borrowing from Latin objectivus. See objet and -if.

panne.e: From Middle French panne, from Old French penne (“fur, especially for lining garments”), from Latin pinna (“feather”).

c: Combien de bains prends-tu par semaine ?
Je suis dans la salle de bains.
On ne sort pas ensemble officiellement.
Je pourrais vous renvoyer pour cela.

miller.e: Borrowed from English Miller or Alemannic German Miller.
c: Le Dr Miller souhaite que vous patientiez quelques instants.
Dr. Miller, bir süre beklemenizi istiyor.
Je n'aime pas vraiment les méthodes d'enseignement du professeur Miller.
Profesör Miller'ın öğretim yöntemlerinden gerçekten hoşlanmam.

invitation.e: Learned borrowing from Latin invitātiō. By surface analysis, inviter + -ation.

allemagne.e: Inherited from Middle French Allemaigne, from Old French Alemaigne, from Latin Alemannia. Doublet of Alémanie.

loyer.e: Inherited from Middle French loyer, loiier, loier, from Old French loier, from Latin locārium.

c: Quel est ton jeu de plateau préféré ?
Il retourna la table sur son plateau.

humour.e: From English humour, itself from Old French humor, humour. Doublet of humeur.

c: Je ne regrette pas mes actes.
Vous devriez être responsable de vos actes.

moche.e: From moque, present indicative of moquer (“to mock”).
c: Ces derniers temps, il fait moche.

junior.e: Borrowed from Latin juniorem; Doublet of geindre. Cf. also the inherited Old French oblique case gignor.
c: Martin Luther King Junior était le fils d'un pasteur noir.
Martin Luther King siyah bir papazın oğluydu.

juif.e: Inherited from Middle French juif, backformation from Old French juive, juiue, feminine of juiu, from Latin iūdaeus, from Ancient Greek Ἰουδαῖος (Ioudaîos), from Hebrew יְהוּדִי (y'hudí).

c: Comment puis-je savoir où elle enferme son argent ?
Onun parasını nereye sakladığını nasıl bileceğim?

joseph.e: Etymology tree Biblical Hebrew הוֹסִיף (hosíf)der. Biblical Hebrew יוֹסֵף (yōsēp̄)bor. Ancient Greek Ἰωσήφ (Iōsḗph)bor. Latin Iōsēphusbor.
c: Marie, voici David, frère de Joseph.
Mary, ben Joe'nun erkek kardeşi David.

expression.e: Inherited from Middle French expression, borrowed from Latin expressiōnem (“a pressing out”).

c: Nous devrions envoyer Jordan à l'hôpital.
Nous avons élu M. Jordan président.

race.e: As Middle French rasse (“entirety of ancestors and descendants of the same family or people”), from c.
c: De quelle race est ton chien ?
Cette race de chat n'a pas de queue.

injuste.e: Borrowed from Latin injūstus. Equivalent to in- + juste.

pleuvoir.e: Inherited from Old French plovoir, from earlier pluveir, from Vulgar Latin *plovere (with a change in conjugation to *plovēre), from Classical Latin pluere.

trafic.e: Inherited from Middle French trafique, traffique (“commerce, illicit commerce”), from Old French traffic (“commerce”), from Italian traffico.
c: Il y a beaucoup de trafic.

exercice.e: Inherited from Old French exercice (first attested in the early thirteenth century), borrowed from Latin exercitium.

cabine.e: Borrowed from English cabin. Doublet of cabane.
c: Où se trouve la cabine téléphonique la plus proche ?
Y a-t-il une cabine téléphonique près d'ici ?
Bu çevrede halk açık bir telefon var mı?
Les étés j'allais d'habitude à Miami.
Miami est la plus grande ville de Floride.
Je veux que tu me baises même si ça fait mal.
Acıtıyor olsa bile, beni becermeni istiyorum.

populaire.e: From Middle French populaire, a learned borrowing from Latin populāris.

nager.e: Inherited from Old French nagier, inherited from a reduced form of Latin navigāre. Doublet of naviguer, a later borrowing. Displaced Old French noer, from Latin natāre, natō (“to swim”).

énerver.e: Inherited from Middle French enerver, from Latin ēnervāre. By surface analysis, é- + nerf + -er.

furieux.e: Inherited from Old French furieus, borrowed from Latin furiōsus.

jessica.e: Borrowed from English Jessica, popular at the end of the 20th century.

nation.e: Inherited from Middle French nation, from Old French nacion, borrowed from Latin nātiōnem.
c: Chaque nation a sa propre langue.
Toute la nation veut la paix.

for.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dʰwer- Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *dʰwór-o- Proto-Italic *θworom Proto-Italic *fworom Proto-Italic *forom Latin forum French for Inherited from Latin forum; doublet…

traître.e: Inherited from Old French traïtre, nominative singular of traïtor, from an adaptation of Latin traditor.

c: Je te promets de te rendre cette cassette vidéo dans une semaine.
Ben bir hafta içinde bu video kaseti geri getirmeye söz veriyorum.

péché.e: Inherited from Middle French peché, from Old French pechié, from Latin peccātum.
c: Ce n'est pas un péché grave.
Des gens pensent que jouer est un péché.
Bazı insanlar kumar oynamanın bir günah olduğunu düşünüyor.

remise.e: From the verb remettre. Compare mise.

c: Elle lui a dit de ne pas s'exciter.

enregistrement.e: From enregistrer (“to register; to save; to record”) + -ment.
c: Je pense que cet enregistrement est important.

arrangé.e: The adjective follows from the verb.

original.e: Borrowed from Latin orīginālis. Doublet of originel.

c: Il n'y a pas eu d'agression.
La frontière est mince entre affirmation de soi et agression.
Özgüven ve saldırganlık arasında ince bir çizgi vardır.

aile.e: Inherited from Middle French aisle, from Old French aile, from Latin āla (“wing [of animals]”).
c: Elle m'a pris sous son aile.

employer.e: Inherited from Middle French employer, from Old French emploier, emploiier, inherited from Latin implicāre. Doublet of impliquer, a borrowing.

c: Mes papiers étaient dans cette boite.

angle.e: Inherited from Middle French angle, from Old French angle, from Latin angulus, anglus.

participer.e: Inherited from Middle French participer, borrowed from Latin participāre.

neveu.e: Inherited from Old French neveu, from Latin nepōtem, from Proto-Italic *nepōts, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *népōts.

activité.e: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin āctīvitās. By surface analysis, actif + -ité.
c: Nous avons une forte activité et sommes à court de personnel.

coucou.e: Inherited from Old French cucu; onomatopoeic derivative of the call of the cuckoo (bird), coucou, or from Latin cuculus.

bourse.e: Inherited from Old French borse, from Medieval Latin, Late Latin bursa, from Ancient Greek βύρσα (búrsa, “hide”).

poubelle.e: e. chief administrator of Paris), who promulgated an ordinance in 1884 that all apartments should have trash cans.

c: L'âge de l'univers est d'environ 13,75 milliards d'années.

milliard.e: From million, by changing the suffix to -ard.
c: Que ferais-tu si tu avais un milliard de dollars ?
Bir milyar doların olsa ne yaparsın?
Bir milyar yetişkin okuma yazma bilmemektedir.

compétition.e: Borrowed from Late Latin competitiōnem, from Latin competō.

viol.e: Deverbal from violer, from Latin violō (“to violate”).
c: Le viol est un crime horrible.
Le viol est toujours un crime violent.
Tecavüz her zaman bir şiddet suçudur.

coté.e: Spelling variant of Côté, a capitalization of côté. From Middle French costé, from Old French coste, from Latin costa.
c: Tom ne voulait pas s'asseoir à coté de moi.
Je suis heureux que Tom fut à mes cotés.

pouls.e: Inherited from Middle French pouls (an etymologizing spelling with a silent ‹l› alongside pous, poux), from Old French pous, from earlier polz, from Latin pulsus (“beat”), from pellō (“drive, push”).

illégal.e: Borrowed from Medieval Latin illegālis, from Latin legālis. Also il- + légal.

autorité.e: Inherited from Old French autorité, borrowed from Latin auctoritātem.
c: Je ne voulais pas remettre en cause ton autorité.
Ben senin otoritene meydan okumak istemedim.

échelle.e: Inherited from Old French eschale, inherited from Latin scāla. Doublet of escale.

tribu.e: Inherited from Old French tribu, from Latin tribus.
c: C'est le chef de sa tribu depuis 35 ans.
O otuz beş yıldır kabilesinin şefidir.
Il y a pas mal de tribus dans le monde.

comédie.e: From Old French comedie, from Latin cōmoedia, from Ancient Greek κωμῳδία (kōmōidía), from κῶμος (kômos, “revel, carousing”) + either ᾠδή (ōidḗ, “song”) or ἀοιδός (aoidós, “singer, bard”), both from ἀείδω (aeídō, “to sin…
c: Cette comédie m'a vraiment fait rire.
J'étais sûr de recevoir un bon accueil.
Ben iyi bir karşılama almaktan emindim.

pomme.e: Inherited from Middle French pomme, from Old French pome, from Latin pōma, plural of pōmum, reanalyzed as a feminine singular, from Proto-Italic *poomos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂po-h₁ém-os (“taken off”).

autoriser.e: Inherited from Old French auctorisier, from Medieval Latin auctōrizāre. Doublet of octroyer.
c: Je ne peux pas autoriser ça.

taule.e: Alternative form of tôle (a dialectal form of table), which acquired a special meaning. Doublet of tôle and table.
c: « Tu aimes ? » « La bouffe était meilleure en taule. »

absurde.e: ), a borrowing from Latin absurdus (“discordant, incongruous”).

souffrance.e: Inherited from Latin sufferentia. By surface analysis, souffrir + -ance.
c: La souffrance est la destinée des hommes.
Je dois rattraper le temps perdu.

demi-tour.e: First attested in the 17th century. demi- + tour.

indien.e: From Middle French indien, from Old French indien. By surface analysis, Inde + -ien.
c: Mon grand-père était en partie indien.

transformer.e: Inherited from Old French transformer, borrowed from Latin trānsfōrmāre.
c: Dan a transformé sa chambre en un bureau.
Dan yatak odasını bir ofise dönüştürdü.
Ne pouvez-vous pas réparer les dégâts ?

réception.e: Learned borrowing from Latin receptiōnem (“the act of receiving; reception”), from recipiō (“receive”), from re- (“back”) + capiō (“to hold”).
c: Alors, comment était donc cette réception ?

mercredi.e: Inherited from Old French mercredi, from Latin Mercuriī diēs, variant of diēs Mercuriī (“day of Mercury”).

union.e: Inherited from Old French union, borrowed from Late Latin ūniō, ūniōnem (“oneness, unity”), from Latin ūnus (“one”).
c: Ils vécurent une union très heureuse.
Çok mutlu bir evlilik hayatı yaşadılar.
L'avion larguait des bombes sur la ville.
L'ennemi a largué des bombes sur l'usine.

ivre.e: Inherited from Old French yvre, inherited from Latin ēbrius.

témoigner.e: Inherited from Middle French tesmoigner, from Old French tesmoignier, from tesmoing.
c: Je dois témoigner au Tribunal demain.
Notre unique témoin refuse de témoigner.

bah.e: Not well-attested in texts, but of imitative origin nevertheless, similar to bayer (“to gape”). Sense 2 is a denasalized version of "ben".

langage.e: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *dn̥ǵʰwéh₂s Proto-Italic *dn̥ɣwā Latin dingua Latin lingua Proto-Indo-European *-h₂ Proto-Indo-European *-éh₂ Proto-Indo-European *-tós Proto-Indo-European *-eh₂tos Proto-Italic *-ātos…

tunnel.e: Borrowed from English tunnel, itself a borrowing from French tonnelle; hence a reborrowing. Doublet of tonnelle.
c: Notre train est passé dans un long tunnel.
Cet endroit sera le point de départ du tunnel.

pur.e: Inherited from Middle French pur, from Old French pur, from Latin pūrus.

poudre.e: Inherited from Old French poudre, poldre, from Late Latin pulvera, neuter plural based on Latin pulvis m, from Proto-Indo-European *pel- (“dust; flour”).
c: Ne mettez pas le feu au poudre.
Vous devez prendre cette poudre après chaque repas.
Her yemekten sonra bu tozu almak zorundasın.

influence.e: From Old French influence, borrowed from Medieval Latin īnfluentia, from Latin īnfluēns (“flowing in”), present active participle of īnfluō (“flow into”), from in- (“in-”) + fluō (“flow”).

c: O benim üzerimde büyük bir etkiydi.
J'ai quelques biens dans le coffre-fort de l'hôtel.

tarte.e: Variant of tourte, from Late Latin torta.

hauteur.e: Etymology tree French haut Proto-Indo-European *-os Proto-Indo-European *-s Proto-Indo-European *-ōs Proto-Italic *-ōs Latin -ōrem Old French -or Middle French -eur French -eur French hauteur From haut + -eur.

c: La décision finale appartient au président.
